prompt: Here's a NestJS service that got noticeably slower after a small change: to avoid prop-drilling the current user's id and tenant id through several services, we made the shared context provider request-scoped so each request gets its own instance. After deploying, p95 latency climbed and throughput dropped under the exact same load profile, even though none of the actual business logic changed. Walk me through why annotating just one provider caused this app-wide regression, then tell me how you'd optimize it back to baseline while still keeping per-request context properly isolated.
